Module 108 · Operation — 18-module program

Unit 220 — LNG Storage & Dispensingthe unit where the product leaves the plant

Tendrara Micro LNG Facilities — operator training program. The final stage of the process: it receives the LNG the Nitrogen Rejection Unit has spent the day making, stores it near atmospheric pressure and about −160 °C, proves its quality, meters it for custody transfer and loads it into cryogenic trucks. What it cannot keep as liquid leaves as vapour, and that vapour is the feed of Unit 360.

TA-221
the atmospheric LNG tank · 6 200 m³, single containment, flat bottom, perlite insulated, held at about −160 °C
V-221
the separator where the flash is born · PIC-2231 holds its pressure, LIC-2232 its level on the way to the tank
P-221A/B · P-222A/B
four Vanzetti ARTIKA 230-2S submerged cryogenic pumps on two loading stations · duty and standby, 30 kW on a VFD
FT-2212 · FT-2222
the custody-transfer Coriolis meters · the secondary source, because the primary measurement is the weight of the truck

What Module 108 covers

One unit, and it is the end of the plant: the place where LNG stops being a process stream and becomes a load on a truck. A tank at atmospheric pressure, four submerged cryogenic pumps, two loading bays — and an operator standing next to the product with a dead-man in his hand.

  • Start with the tank — flat-bottomed, atmospheric, about −160 °C. Its pressure window is measured in millibar, and it is defended from both sides.
  • Follow the LNG in flow order on one drawing: in from the NRU, down into the tank, out to two stations — and the vapour coming back the other way.
  • Open the pump. A submerged machine with no mechanical seal: the feed-through connector is the only place a leak can come from, and that changes what you inspect.
  • Then the operating day — every cooldown at −40 °C/h, the dead-man, and the two pressure limits on the tanker.
  • Finish outside the fence line. This unit hangs off Unit 360 through the boil-off loop, and one trip on this tank closes a valve in that unit.

Block 1 · before any operating detail — unit 220 LNG transfer area · classified hazardous area

The hazards of this unit

One product, four distinct risks: the cold, the fire, the pressure it makes when it warms, and the air it displaces.

1 · the cold
≈ −160 °C
  • Cryogenic burns — fluid, cold surfaces, cold vapour
  • A cold line looks identical to an ambient one
  • Embrittlement: carbon steel fractures — cold service is stainless
2 · fire & explosion
FLAMMABLE GAS
  • Released gas in a classified hazardous area
  • Every installed item certified for explosive atmospheres
  • Nothing uncertified crosses the boundary — pockets included
3 · trapped liquid
LIQUID → GAS
  • Blocked-in LNG warms and expands
  • Liquid sections carry TSV reliefs set at 5 / 15 barg
  • Boil-off vapour is recovered to the BOG header, not vented
4 · the air
OXYGEN DEFICIT
  • Escaping vapour displaces oxygen — and has no odour
  • Cold vapour is denser than air: it lies low until it warms
  • The visible cloud is moisture — gas reaches beyond it
the area answersGD ×4gas detectionFD ×4flame detectionSD ×2smoke detectionESD ×6mushroom & emergency pushbuttonsXL-220-ES7ESD beacon
If you are not trained, not authorised, or not familiar with these procedures, do not operate any equipment.contact your HSE supervisor before performing any operation in this system

V-221 — where the flash is born

The LNG is let down before it gets here, and a pressure drop on a saturated liquid boils part of it — that is the flash. V-221 is horizontal, holds 1,33 m³, and does one job: vapour off through PV-2231, liquid on to the tank, with the level held by LV-2232 — a valve that sits on the next sheet, drawn here anyway so both loops close on one face.

V-221 — drawn to the data block, 800 mm bore by 2 500 mm TL to TL■ LG liquid · ■ BG vapour · ■ safety family
Block 2 · three layers, two directions, and one empty cell — manual §4.4 (pages 31–33) · Tables 4.5 and 4.8 · registers on PRO13-ING-PR26

Tank pressure — defended on both sides

TA-221 stores at near-atmospheric pressure: pump liquid out and it falls, let heat in and it rises. Each direction has its own defence — but not the same number of them, and that gap is the face.

TA-221 — the same section as face 13, with the pressure side lit and the filling greyed back■ safety family · ■ ESD · □ PCS
◀◀ pressure FALLING — pump the liquid out and it drops
pressure RISING — let the heat in and it climbs ▶▶
1 · CONTROLPCS
PIC-2202 on PT-2202 (PCS, 0–200 mbarg, SP 150) opens XV-2203 — on/off, fail OPEN, ZSH/ZSL-2203 — to the PBUC, and back in as gas. No pump.
PV-2201, pressure reducing valve, BOG pressure control: the 6in vent to Unit 360. The routine outlet — it works every day.
2 · TRIPESD
THERE IS NONE. The three trips on this vessel are LAHH-2201 (PSD), LALL-2201 (LSD) and PAHH-2201 (LSD) — not one is low pressure.
PT-2201 (ESD) → PAHH-2201 → LSD closes SDV-2201, SDV-2202 and XV-3601 at once. No falling back to the other feed.
3 · RELIEFmechanical
The same bodies, breathing in: every set on the right is a pair — −2,2 mmH₂O on A and B, −2,5 on C.
PSV-2201A / B 200 / −2,2 mmH₂O inner tank · PSV-2201C 4,5 / −2,5 and PSE-2201 5 mmH₂O interspace · TSV-2201/02 abnormal only, TSV-2202 CLOSED in normal operation.
NOT A LAYER — nitrogen through PCV-2201 / PCV-2202 (GCE-Charledave A102), PT-2203 (−50/50 mbarg, PCS), PG-2204 and FI-2201 / FI-2202: supervision and alarm only, no part of any automatic pressure control loop (manual §4.4). Nobody is holding that blanket for you.
Block 2 · the tank in section, from the P&ID — PR26 · vendor nozzle schedule · manual §4.4 (pages 31–32)

Filling the tank

One tee, and two nozzles that both enter through the roof: A drops a pipe down the inside to discharge under the liquid, B stops at the roof. Nothing pumps it — the separator sits at a pressure the tank does not.

TA-221 — the atmospheric LNG tank

A single-containment, flat-bottom, atmospheric cryogenic LNG tank — API 620 and EN 14620, perlite insulated, storing at near-atmospheric pressure and ≈ −160 °C.

Two walls — only the inner one is built for the liquid. It lives in a window a fifth of one bar wide, and it is defended from below as well as from above.

Where the numbers come from: the construction sentence and the ≈ −160 °C are manual §4.4; the dimensions and the two design pressures are the data block of PRO13-ING-PR26, and the vendor general arrangement agrees on both pressures independently. Perlite is a process variable: heat that gets through it becomes boil-off the BOG system then has to handle — the insulation is not a building material, it is part of the process.

Block 3 · a closed discharge and a starved suction both kill it — manual §4.7.1 Table 4.11 (pages 47–49) · §4.7.3 · S-222 is the mirror with 222X tags

The interlocks that protect the pump

Two ways to destroy this machine without meaning to: run it against a closed discharge, or run it below its minimum flow. Each protection is drawn where it acts.

The protections, on the process they protect■ permissive · ■ minimum flow · ■ overpressure
■  PERMISSIVE · PV-2211
the controller will not start the pump unless the discharge valve is confirmed open — that is what avoids dead-head
■  MINIMUM FLOW · BYPASS
asked for less than the pump's minimum continuous flow, part of the liquid recirculates to TA-221 to hold it
■  OVERPRESSURE · PAHH-2216
forces PV-2215 open and diverts the LNG back to the tank — the relief path of this line is TA-221, not the air
■  HEALTH · the differential
discharge minus suction: the controller computes the pump differential to monitor and protect the machine

Block 4 · more than every other valve family put together — Table 4.5 (pages 35–38) · valve register · manual §4.4

Why 38 thermal safety valves

Because liquid at −160 °C shut in between two closed valves has nowhere to go. The count is not caution: it is a census of isolatable segments.

The mechanism — one trapped segment, three moments■ yellow = safety family
The census — 38 thermal safety valves by what they protect■ yellow = safety family · all 38 of them
A habit worth taking away: before you close the second valve on a section, know where its thermal relief is. A blind fitted in the wrong place removes the protection this whole design assumes — and TSV-2202 shall remain closed during normal operation (manual §4.4), so seeing either tank valve open means the unit already has a problem.
Block 4 · the same word, three orders of magnitude apart — Table 4.5 (pages 35–37) · valve register · manual §4.4

The relief set of the tank

Fourteen relief devices, and the column that matters is units. An atmospheric tank lives in a window a few millibar wide, so it is protected in millimetres of water — and every one of its sets is a pair.

The relief set — the span, and the pairs■ yellow = safety family · red = the vacuum half

Read the drawing number with the tag. Which machine a relief belongs to is settled by the valve register and the sheet it sits on — the 2231/2233 pairs are on the S-222 sheet and 2251A/B on the separator sheet, whatever the tag numbering suggests at first glance. And the tank devices only ever act at the extreme: they discharge to atmosphere only in abnormal or emergency conditions (manual §4.4).
Block 4 · the solenoid is where the command lands — valve register · `plant_valves` unit 220 · Table 4.5 (page 37)

Solenoids and on-off valves

Every valve that moves on command has a solenoid, and the register says which system owns it. Fifteen on-off valves, fifteen PCS solenoids paired to them one to one by number, and three on the ESD.

The same symbol twice — and only the family changes it□ white = process · ■ yellow = safety family
familynsystemsignalwhat it drives
XV-… on-off bodies15——the valve body itself — pneumatic
XEV-… solenoids15PCSDOone per XV, same number
SDEV-2201/22022ESDDOthe two tank-inlet shutdown valves
LEV-22321ESDDOLV-2232 — a control valve
ASCO I&M 123 620 793X · the solenoid box in the metal: coil around the core tube · Ex d IIC · IP66/67
The one worth remembering is LEV-2232. The other two ESD solenoids sit on shutdown valves, which is what you would expect — this one sits on a control valve, so the shutdown system can take the separator level valve away from its controller. And note what the register does not record for the fifteen on-off valves: no system and no signal. Only the solenoid carries those, because the solenoid is the electrical half. In safety terms: SDV / SDEV / LEV are the safety family; XV and XEV are process on-off — they close because the sequence says so, not because a trip does.

liquid level — unit 220 · keeping NPSHa above NPSHr

Liquid level in operation

One criterion governs the whole operation: NPSHa above NPSHr. The operator has two levers on it, and one of them is not the level.

Figure 4.7 (b) · pump installation and hydraulic conditionsredrawn · manual §4.7.4
level
Minimum normal operating level is the return line connection, 1 195 mm above ground level.
PBUC
A PBUC pressure of 200 mbar above the actual vapour pressure adds about 4,5 m of NPSHa, taking a liquid density of 450 kg/m³.
permissive
LALL-2201 on LT-2201 inhibits pump start at low level. Start is permitted again only once the minimum level condition is restored.
and level is not only about NPSH
  • It keeps proper lubrication of the rotating components - bearings, DU bushings and the rest.
  • It keeps adequate cooling of the motor windings. A submerged motor is cooled by the liquid it sits in.
Where NPSH is measured, and it is not the nozzle: the reference datum is the inducer inlet, 150 mm from the pump suction nozzle. A temperature probe on the pump return, TT-2213, watches the thermal condition for pump cooling. Source: unit manual section 4.7.4, Liquid Level, and Figure 4.7, pages 52-53.
Block 5 · the station is not operated by eye — manual §4.7.5–§4.7.8 (Tables 4.13–4.16) · Table 4.12, field panel components · two bays, S-221 and S-222

The four procedures, and who does each step

Four written procedures, run in this order — each one says when it is used and why, every step says who does it, and the tags come in two sets: S-221 for bay 1, S-222 for bay 2.

cooldown — unit 220 · suction line, seven manual steps

Suction line cooldown

The first of the four, and the only manual one — and the manual says why that matters: continuous operator attention is required.

cooldown — unit 220 · discharge line, fourteen actions and one of them is yours

Discharge cooldown

The operator throws one switch. Everything after it is a system command — and that colour flip, top right, is the whole difference from the suction line.

cooldown — unit 220 · the truck, and the meter

Truck cooldown

Cooling a truck spends LNG, and that LNG is somebody’s. This procedure exists to account for it — which is why it starts by zeroing the meters and ends at a save button.

2The tank is atmosphericmbarg, not barg
  • Its pressure window is 0–200 mbarg on PIC-2202 — millibars, not bars.
  • Defended from below by the PBUC, from above by the vent and the PSVs.
  • That pressure is an operating tool: +200 mbar is worth about +4,5 m of NPSHa at ρ = 450 kg/m³.
  • The physical floor under it is the return connection at 1 195 mm.
3One trip chain, by heartit leaves Unit 220
  • PAHH-2201 → LSD closes SDV-2201 and SDV-2202…
  • …and XV-3601, which belongs to Unit 360. The chain does not stop at the unit boundary.
  • LALL-2201 trips all four loading pumps.
  • Learn it in that order: what measures, what it closes, what it stops.
4No mechanical sealone leak point
  • It is submerged in the liquid it pumps. The feed-through connector is the only place a leak can come from.
  • The cryostat drains through its own valve, 221-HV-018.
  • There is no periodic maintenance: a pump leaves service when an inspection finds one of the four symptoms, not on a calendar.
5Cool-down has one number−40 °C/h
  • The suction line runs the ramp on TT-2213 down to −165 °C.
  • The discharge runs the same ramp on TT-2217 to its own imposed setpoint.
  • It is a limit, not a target. Rushing it is how you crack something.
6Loading is invoicingthe last press
  • Dead-man in your hand for the whole transfer.
  • 12 m³/h to start, 60 m³/h once it is stable.
  • ≤10 bar in the truck; ≤1 bar before you disconnect.
  • The last press is Save Truck Loading Operation — that is what makes the load exist.
7Thermal safety valves38 of them
  • Cryogenic liquid trapped between two closed valves always leaves by some route.
  • The TSV is the route you chose.
  • So the habit is one question: if you close two valves on a cryogenic line, what happens to what you just trapped between them?
Where the rest lives — every operating procedure of this unit is a numbered table in section 4.7 of the manual, and faces 33–37 print them. Find §4.7 and you can find the step you have forgotten. Next — questions, then the exam.
